bullets.title: ADBE F2Q26: Beat + Raised Guide, But Stock -6% on CFO Departure & CEO Vacancy
bullets.body: Adobe reported Q2 revenue of $6.62B (+13% Y/Y, +3% vs. consensus $6.45B) and EPS of $5.96 (+2% vs. $5.82 consensus); total ARR of $27.10B grew 12.5% Y/Y including $480M from SemRush. FY26 revenue guidance raised to $26.50-26.60B and EPS to $24.35-24.45. Despite the clean beat-and-raise, stock fell ~6% AH as CFO Dan Durn departs June 15 to join MRVL (interim CFO Steve Day), and CEO position remains unfilled. Wolfe reiterates Outperform with $320 PT, noting organic ARR growth slowing to 8.6% to fund freemium Firefly/Express/Acrobat AI strategy.

bullets.title: MRVL: Appoints Dan Durn (ex-Adobe CFO) as New CFO; KeyBanc Positive, PT Under Review
bullets.body: Marvell Technology named Dan Durn as incoming CFO effective June 15, replacing Willem Meintjes (stepping down immediately, staying in advisory role through April 2027). Durn brings deep semi-industry experience from Applied Materials, NXP, and GFS and was already on MRVL's board since 2024. KeyBanc maintains Overweight; PT under review based on 42x FY28 EPS of $6.16 (vs. current 45x). Company reaffirmed Q2 FY27 guidance provided May 27.

bullets.title: ORCL: -8-11% on $70B FY27 Capex & $40B Capital Raise Plans; Street Fears ROI/Margin Headwinds
bullets.body: Oracle fell 8-11% after FQ4 results showed strong RPO growth (+363% Y/Y) but raised FY27 capex to $70B and announced plans to raise $40B in additional capital for AI data center build-out; Street concerned about ROI timelines and margin headwinds. Oracle bonds rallied after the company signaled no additional issuance this year. Separately, ORCL announced a ~$396M OPM federal contract for HR modernization replacing 100+ legacy systems.

bullets.title: INTC: BofA Upgrades to Buy, Raises PT to $135 from $96 on Leading-Edge Wafer/Packaging Opportunity
bullets.body: Bank of America upgraded Intel to Buy from Underperform and raised its price target to $135 from $96, citing leading-edge wafer and packaging opportunities. AMD separately claimed 15 of 15 top CPU spots on Amazon's best-seller list, shutting Intel out, though BofA's thesis focuses on Intel's foundry and AI packaging angle rather than consumer CPU market share.

bullets.title: RBRK: Wolfe Reiterates Outperform, $95 PT (33% Upside) on AI Platform Expansion & 20%+ Cloud NNARR Growth
bullets.body: Wolfe Research reiterates Outperform on Rubrik with $95 PT after Analyst Day, highlighting the company's repositioning from cyber resilience vendor to Security and AI Operations platform. Cloud NNARR has grown 20%+ for five consecutive quarters vs. Street estimates of ~10% FY27 growth. RBRK trades at ~7x CY27 EV/S vs. scaled-leader comps at ~10x and Data/Infra/Security at ~14x, and is down only 7% YTD vs. IGV -14%.

bullets.title: FSLR +8.8%, OKLO +7.1%, ENPH +8.6% on Renewables Strength & Nuclear Approval
bullets.body: Renewables surged broadly: FSLR jumped 8.8% as UBS raised its PT to $330 from $290 on expected Section 232 polysilicon tariff resolution by July; OKLO gained 7.1% after DOE approved the Aurora reactor safety analysis, targeting criticality by July 4; ENPH rose 8.6% and VST +5.7% in the broad renewable rally.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Home Listing Ads Nationwide Rollout — Structural Threat to Portals, Modest Near-Term Revenue Upside
bullets.body: Google launched for-sale home listing ads nationwide using MLS data with broker tour links, and is developing an agentic AI real estate strategy via Gemini. Morgan Stanley sees near-term insulation for Zillow (80% direct traffic) but long-term risk if agentic tools redirect ad dollars. At 3% penetration and 6% take rate, the feature adds ~1% (~$3B) to GOOGL's 2027 search revenues, rising to ~3% at higher penetration. EXPE/BKNG analog from Google Flights suggests limited structural disruption near-term.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY Market Share Declining; GGR -51% Y/Y Weekly Amid Hold Rate Compression
bullets.body: DraftKings' weekly GGR in New York fell 51% Y/Y (handle +4%) for the week ending June 7, with 2Q26-to-date GGR down 7% Y/Y and market share slipping to 32% from 35%. FanDuel also soft (-42% weekly GGR). The weakness is partially hold-rate driven (FanDuel -691bps, DraftKings -690bps weekly). Fanatics continues to gain share with 2Q26TD GGR +33% Y/Y.

bullets.title: RH Q1 Beat on Margins, But Q2 Revenue Guide +0.5-2.5% Misses Consensus +4.6%
bullets.body: Restoration Hardware reported Q1 revenue of $800.3M (vs. $792.5M consensus), adjusted EBITDA of $56.9M (vs. $48.8M), and EPS of ($1.97) vs. ($2.12) consensus. Q2 revenue guidance of +0.5-2.5% Y/Y was below the +4.6% Street expectation; FY guidance of +4.5-8.0% was roughly in line. UBS flagged the headline beat likely creates a short squeeze despite FCF of only $13M easing balance sheet concerns.

bullets.title: META: Ends Manus Partnership After Chinese Regulatory Demand; MSFT Down on Xbox Layoffs
bullets.body: Meta terminated its partnership with Chinese AI company Manus following demands from Chinese regulators. Microsoft fell ~1.8% on reports of major layoffs planned in its Xbox business. MSFT also restricted employee access to Claude Fable citing data retention concerns.

bullets.title: NVDA: Drives 14% of S&P 500 Move Wednesday; DLSS Critical for Switch 2; Healthcare AI Partnership
bullets.body: NVDA accounted for 14% of the S&P 500's daily move on June 10. Jensen Huang appeared in media emphasizing deep AI adoption. NVIDIA DLSS is described as the critical enabling tech for Nintendo Switch 2 performance. Separately, NVDA is developing a healthcare AI model with startup Abridge for medical note-taking per WSJ.

bullets.title: KKR/NVDA/VST Launch $10B+ Helix Digital Infrastructure AI Data Center Fund
bullets.body: KKR launched Helix Digital Infrastructure with more than $10B in committed capital anchored by NVIDIA, Vistra, and Kuwait Investment Authority. Separately, BX and APO are backing AVGO in an AI XPV Platform with a $35B initial tranche targeting more than 20GW of compute capacity.

bullets.title: CVNA: Morgan Stanley Reiterates OW, $102 PT; IRCs Generate $94M OP Year 1 With Capital-Light Path to 5M Units
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight on Carvana with $102 PT, detailing that individual reconditioning centers cost $45-80M and generate $94M operating profit in Year 1 with 60K-unit capacity. Capex is under 1% of sales; CVNA is forecast to generate ~$15B FCF FY26-FY30 while spending only $2.5B capex. Citi also flagged CVNA web traffic +61% Y/Y (accelerating +3pts) as a positive traffic indicator.

bullets.title: GOOGL Traffic Trends Strong in May; Search Share +50bps M/M to 90.5% Globally
bullets.body: Citi's May internet traffic analysis highlights GOOGL global search share rising 50bps M/M to 90.5% (U.S. +60bps to ~86%). DASH U.S. MAUs +6% Y/Y, ABNB +10% Y/Y, UBER +8% Y/Y, RDDT U.S. visits +7% Y/Y. Meta core app MAUs declined 1.3% Y/Y in May vs. +0.3% prior month, though Instagram time spent at 60 mins/DAU (+4% M/M) remains strong. Citi's top picks include AMZN, GOOGL, DASH, CVNA, RDDT.

bullets.title: HF Flows: Semis Bought +3z, Software Sold; Mag 7 Saw -2.3z Long-Side Selling Last Week
bullets.body: Goldman prime brokerage weekly wrap shows HF net leverage fell 4% to 8th percentile on 12-month basis with US positioning below -2z on 1-week change vs. recent ATH above +2z. Semis reversed last week's selling with +3z and +2z net buying over two days; Hardware bought +1.7z. US Software sold -1.8z last week but reversed positively this week. Mag 7 saw -2.3z long-side selling and -0.8z short covering. Financials shifted from most-sold to most-bought, with S&P Financials averaging +3.3% in July over last 10 years.

bullets.title: TTD: Walmart Expanding DSP Partnerships, Contradicting Trade Desk CEO's Competitive Landscape Comments
bullets.body: Walmart is embracing more demand-side platforms, which a market observer notes contradicts Trade Desk CEO Jeff Green's prior statements that the competitive landscape is not intensifying. No price target or rating change, but directionally negative for TTD's narrative around exclusive supply-side positioning.

bullets.title: NOW: ServiceNow-IBM Partnership Targets Enterprise AI Data and Legacy App Barriers
bullets.body: ServiceNow and IBM announced a partnership to address the AI-ready data problem and legacy application layer as barriers to enterprise AI at scale — two of the most commonly cited obstacles to broad adoption. No financial terms disclosed.

bullets.title: TSLA: Oppenheimer Lifts Estimates on Stronger EV Demand; Iran Threatens Elon Musk's Middle East Companies
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised Tesla estimates citing improved product lineup, stronger EV demand, and ongoing cost reductions driving higher vehicle and energy storage sales forecasts. Separately, Iranian state media threatened Elon Musk's Middle East operations including Tesla, though no financial impact was quantified.

bullets.title: AMD Pre-Quiet Period IR Call Jun 12; AMD Claims 15/15 Amazon Top CPU Best-Sellers
bullets.body: JPMorgan scheduled an AMD pre-quiet period discussion with the IR team for June 12 at 10:30am ET. AMD's marketing chief separately claimed 15 of 15 top CPU slots on Amazon's best-seller list, shutting Intel out entirely — though Intel's BofA upgrade thesis focuses on foundry/packaging, not consumer CPUs.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT: Hyperscalers Are Key OBBBA Tax Beneficiaries; FCF Could Surprise +1%+ in 2026
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the One Big Beautiful Budget Act restores bonus depreciation, immediate R&D expensing, and FDDEI, which could lift S&P 500 FCF by 1%+ in 2026. Hyperscalers like AMZN, GOOGL, and MSFT are the primary beneficiaries given large R&D deductions and bonus depreciation on AI capex. Median cash tax rates fell ~3% in 2025 with further relief expected in 2026.
